भद्रमना: Bhadramanā f.: A mythical female elephant (?). One of the nine self-born (आत्मसं-भवा) daughters of Krodhavaśā (or of Tāmrā (?) 1. 60. 54; in that case क्रोधवशा ‘irascible’); the divine lordly elephant Airā-vata her son 1. 60. 58, 61.
भासी: Bhāsī f.: A mythical being. One of the five daughters of divine (देवी) Tāmrā, she gave birth to vultures (गृध्रस्) and other birds of prey (भासस्) 1. 60. 54, 55; also mentioned as one of the seven (eight ?) daughters of divine (देवी) Prāvā 1. 59. 44, 47.
भूलिङ्गशकुनि: Bhūliṅgaśakuni f.: Name of a female bird. Lives on the other side of Himavant; re-puted to utter cries which sound like मा-साहसम् ‘do not commit a rash act’, but herself acts rashly; she, a dull-witted bird, tries to pick out pieces of flesh stuck between the teeth of a lion when he is eating flesh; obviously she lives at the pleasure of the lion; hence cited as an example for those who, while living at the pleasure of others, act rashly but tell others not to do so; according to Śiśupāla Bhīṣma acted like this Bhūliṅga-śakuni when he praised Kṛṣṇa 2. 41. 18-23.
भैरव: Bhairava m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the family of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 15, 13.
भार्गवास्त्र: Bhārgavāstra nt.: Name of a missile. Obtained by Karṇa from Bhārgava (Rāma Jāmadagnya) 8. 51. 101; described as fearful (घोर, घोररूप) 8. 51. 101, 102, very fierce (सुदारुण) 8. 51. 102; difficult to resist (दुर्निवार) 8. 51. 104; cannot be resisted in war (नैतद् अस्त्रं हि समरे शक्यं हन्तुं कथंचन) 8. 45. 46; flaming with its lustre (ज्वलति स्वेन तेजसा) 8. 51. 102; hence burning the oppo-nent's armies (तापनं सर्वसैन्यानाम्) 8. 51. 102; compared with the thunderbolt of Indra (शक्रेणेव महाशनिम्) 8. 52. 6; used by Karṇa against the Pāñcāla and the Pāṇḍava armies when the Kaurava soldiers took to their heels 8. 45. 34; as a result crores and प्रयुतस् and अर्बुदस् of sharp arrows were released from the Bhārgavāstra; the armies were tortured by the arrows which were burning and which were sped by their feathers of the Kaṅka birds 8. 45. 35-37; thousands of warriors, elephants, chariots and horses fell down due to the impact of the missile 8. 45. 38; 8. 51. 99-100; Arjuna pointed out to Kṛṣṇa the havoc created by the might of the Bhārgavāstra 8. 45. 45-46; the Pāñcāla army withdrew what they never had done before 8. 51. 95-99; 8. 52. 5-6.
भास्कर: Bhāskara astra nt.: Name of a missile. Abhimanyu employed (प्रादुष्कृ-) it to dispel the dense darkness produced by the great माया (महामाया) of the Rakṣas Alambusa; the Bhāskara astra destroyed the माया and there was light everywhere 6. 97. 21-24.
भौम: Bhauma astra nt.: Name of a missile. While displaying his skill in the use of missiles, Arjuna employed Bhauma astra and entered the earth (भौमेन प्राविशद् भू-मिं) 1. 125. 20.
भ्रान्त: Bhrānta nt.: One of the twenty-one movements (मार्ग) used by a swordsman. Dhṛṣṭadyumna used it when he, with a sword and a shield in hand, wanted to attack Drona who was shooting arrows at him 7. 164. 145-148.
भगवद्गीता: Bhagavadgītā f.: Name of the 63rd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 56, 33, 70. In it the highly intelligent Vāsudeva destroyed the turbidity of mind of Pārtha (Arjuna), arising out of confusion, by advanc-ing arguments which taught the way that led to liberation (कश्मलं यत्र पार्थस्य वासुदेवो महामतिः । मोहजं नाशयाम् आस हेतुभिर् मोक्षदर्शनैः) 1. 2. 156; the incident is referred to in the summary of the events made by Dhṛtarāṣṭra for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 124 and by Vaiśaṃpāyana at 12. 336. 8 (समुपोढेष्व् अनीकेषु कुरुपाण्डवयोर् मृधे । अर्जुने विमनस्के च गीता भग-वता स्वयम्); the पर्वन् is related to the अध्यायस् 6. 14 (in fact 23)-40.
भगवद्यान: Bhagavadyāna nt.: Name of the 54th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 51, 33, 70. Listed in the contents of the Udyoga-parvan as follows: where Kṛṣṇa, overcome by compassion and desiring peace, himself went to Hāstinapura, but his proposal, which was beneficial to both the parties, was rejected by Duryodhana; where, having come to know the evil design of Karṇa, Duryodhana and others, Kṛṣṇa manifested his mastery over the divine power to the assembled kings (योगेश्वरत्वं कृष्णेन यत्र राजसु दर्शितम्) 1. 2. 145-147; referred to by Dhṛtarāṣṭra in his summary of the events made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 118-120; the sub-पर्वन् comprises the अध्यायस् 5. 70-137.
भविष्यत्: Bhaviṣyat nt.: Name of the 100th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 69, 33, 70. Also mentioned at the end of the listing of the contents of the eighteen major पर्वन्स् as one of the two supplements of the Bhārata (खिलेषु हरिवंशश् च भविष्यच् च प्रकीर्तितम्) 1. 2. 233; described as highly wonderful among the Khilas (खिलेष्व् एवाद्भुतं महत्) 1. 2. 69; related to the अध्यायस् 114-118 of the Harivaṃśa.
भारत: Bhārata, Mahābhārata nt.: Name of the great epic composed by Vyāsa, who was also known as Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana; the title Bhārata once given to an abridgement of the original in 24000 श्लोकस् made by dropping the उपाख्यानस् (चतुर्विंशति-साहस्रीम् चक्रे भारतसंहिताम् । उपा-ख्यानैर् विना तावद् भारतं प्रोच्यते बुधैः ॥ ) 1. 1. 61; also called Bhāratī kathā (श्रोतुं पात्रं च राजंस् त्वं प्राप्येमां भारतीं कथाम्) 1. 55. 3. A. Contents and definition: It nar-rates the extensive life-story of the Kurus (कुरूणां चरितं महत्) 1. 56. 1, or the full story of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas (कुरूणां चरितं कृत्स्नम् पाण्डवानां च भारत) 18. 5. 25; or the history of Śaṃtanu (यस्य (i. e. शंतनोः) इतिहासो द्युतिमान् महाभारतम् उच्यते) 1. 93. 46; Vaiśaṃpāyana summarized for Jana-mejaya its contents in three words, ‘breach, loss of kingdom, and victory’ (एवम् एतत् पुरावृत्तं तेषाम् अक्लिष्टकर्मणाम् । भेदो राज्यविनाशश् च जयश् च जयतां वर) 1. 55. 43 (also cf. 1. 55. 4-5 where the three events are referred to as भेद, वनवास and युद्ध); earlier the three events are referred to by a single word भेद (कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च यथा भेदो ऽभवत् पुरा) 1. 54. 22, or by two भेद and राज्यविनाश (भेदं राज्यविनाशं च कुरुपाण्डवयोस् तदा) 1. 54. 24; the sage (Vyāsa) examined together the शास्त्रस् related to Dharma, Kāma and Artha, as also other शास्त्रस्, and the laws that govern the affairs of the world; next also the histories with their commen-taries and different revealed texts; all that is included here—this defines the text (of the Mahābhārata) (धर्मकामार्थ-शास्त्राणि शास्त्राणि विविधानि च । लोकयात्रा-विधानं च संभूतं दृष्टवान् ऋषिः ॥ इतिहासाः सवैयाख्या विविधाः श्रुतयो ऽपि च । इह सर्वम् अनुक्रान्तम् उक्तं ग्रन्-थस्य लक्षणम् 1. 1. 47-48. B. Charac-terizations: (i) आख्यान (once उपाख्यान 1. 2. 236) 1. 1. 16 (°वरिष्ठ); 1. 2. 29, 30, 195, 235, 238-241, 243; 1. 53. 31, 32, 35; 1. 56. 1, 30, 32; 12. 331. 2; 12. 334. 11; 12. 337. 10; 18. 5. 53; (ii) इतिहास 1. 1. 17, 24, 52; 1. 2. 31, 32 (°उत्तम), 33, 237 (°उत्तम) 1. 54. 23 (पुरातन); 1. 56. 16, 18, 1. 93. 46 (द्युतिमन्त्); 18. 5. 31 (पुण्यो ऽयम् इतिहासाख्यः), 43 (पुण्य); (iii) पुराण 1. 1. 15; 1. 56. 15 (पुराणं ऋषिसंस्तुतम्); (iv) कथा 1. 53. 28, 33; 1. 55. 3 (Bhāratī kathā); 1. 56. 2 (चित्रार्-था); 12. 334. 4; (v) चरित (कुरूणां चरितं महत्) 1. 56. 1; (vi) (fifth) Veda 1. 1. 204, 205 (कार्ष्ण वेद); 1. 56. 17 (कार्ष्ण वेद); 1. 57. 74 (वेदान् … महाभारतपञ्चमान्); (vii) संहिता 1. 1. 19 (व्यासस्याद्भुतकर्मणः । सं-हिताम्); 1. 1. 61 (भारतसंहिता); 1. 57. 75 (संहितास् तैः पृथक्त्वेन भारतस्य प्रकाशिताः; Nī., however on Bom. Ed. 1. 1. 253: ब्रह्मात्मैकत्वविद्याप्रतिपादकं ग्रन्-थं सूत्रवृत्त्योः प्राग् उक्तयोर् वार्तिकस्था-नीयम् उपनिषच्छब्दवाच्यम् अब्रवीत्); (ix) मत 1. 1. 23 (प्रवक्ष्यामि मतं कृत्स्नं व्यासस्यामिततेजसः); 1. 55. 2; 1. 56. 12; 1. 53. 35 (कृष्णद्वैपायनमतं महाभारतम्); (x) composition (सन्दर्-भ) described as ‘not received by tradition’ i. e. ‘original’ (?) (अनागतं … कृष्णद्वै-पायनः प्रभुः । संदर्भं भारत-स्यास्य कृतवान् धर्मकाम्यया) 18. 5. 41. C. Author: The great epic composed by the great sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, also called Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī 1. 1. 9-10 (कृष्णद्वैपायनप्रोक्ताः … कथाः … महाभारतसंश्रिताः); 1. 1. 15 (द्वै-पायनेन यत् प्रोक्तं पुराणम्); 1. 1. 19 (व्यासस्याद्भुतकर्मणः । संहिताम्); 1. 1. 52 (इतिहासम् इमं चक्रे पुण्यं सत्यवतीसुतः); 1. 1. 56 (महान् ऋषिः not named); 1. 1. 60 (भगवान् ऋषिः not named); came out of the lips of Dvaipāyana (द्वैपायनोष्ठपुटनिःसृतम्) 1. 2. 242 18. 5. 54; 1. 53. 28 (व्याससंपन्नाम्); 1. 53. 35 (कृष्णद्वैपायनमतम्); 1. 56. 12 (मतं कृत्स्नं व्यासस्य); 1. 56. 13 (सत्यवत्यात्मजेनेह व्याख्यातम् 1. 56. 15 (पुराणम् ऋषिसंस्तुतम् sage not named); 1. 56. 21 (प्रोक्तं व्यासेन); 1. 56. 25 (कृष्णद्वैपायनेनेदं कृतम्); fully engrossed, the sage composed it in three years (त्रिभिर् वर्सैः सदोत्थायी कृष्णद्वै-पायनो मुनिः । महाभारतम् आख्यानं कृतवान्) 1. 56. 32, 18. 5. 41; 12. 334. 9 (कृष्णद्वैपायनं व्यासं विद्धि नारा-यणं प्रभुम् । को ह्य् अन्यः पुरुषव्या-घ्र महाभारत्कृद् भवेत्); having com-posed it at the foot of the mountain Hima-vant the sage (not named) was tired by the strenuous activity (? तपः) of composing the आख्यान (हिमवत्पाद आसतः ॥ कृत्वा भारतम् आख्यानं तपःश्रान्तस्य धी-मतः) 12. 337. 9-10; 18. 5. 31 (कृष्णेन मुनिना); 18. 5. 46 (महर्षिर् भगवान् व्यासः कृत्वेमां संहितां पुरा); the sage Kṛṣṇa (Vyāsa) who is described as gifted with divine sight (दिव्यचक्षुः 18. 5. 7) and supersensory power (कृष्णेन … अतीन्द्रियेण 18. 5. 31-32) composed it having seen it with his divine eye (दृष्ट्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा) 18. 5. 33; Vyāsa had assured Dhṛtarāṣṭra that he would proclaim the fame of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas 6. 2. 13; the sage is also credited to have made the Parvasaṃgraha listing a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata (एतत् पर्वशतं पूर्णं व्यासेनोक्तं महात्मना) 1. 2. 70. D. Etymology: So called because of its extent (? impor-tance ?) and weight (महत्त्वाद् भारवत्त्वाच् च महाभारतम् उच्यते । निरुक्तम् अस्य यो वेद) 1. 1. 209; so called because it contains the great life-story (?) of the Bhāratas (भारतानां महज् जन्म महा-भारतम् उच्यते । निरुक्तम् अस्य यो वेद) 1. 56. 31. E. Extent: One hundred thousand श्लोकस् 1. 56. 13 (इदं शतसहस्-रं हि श्लोकानां पुण्यकर्मणाम्); 12. 331. 2 (इदं शतसहस्राद् धि भारता-ख्यानविस्तरात्). F. Abridgements: Its abridgements are referred to in 1. 1. 25 (विस्तरैश् च समासैश् च धार्यते यद् द्विजातिभिः); the sage himself is credited with an abridgement of the store of know-ledge after he had first expounded it in full; learned men desire to preserve it in full as well as in abridgement (विस्तीर्यैतन् महज् ज्ञानम् ऋषिः संक्षेपम् अब्रवीत् । इष्तं हि विदुसां लोके समासव्यासधारनम्) 1. 1. 49; the sage Dvaipāyana abridged (the full extent of one hundred thousand श्लोकस् into 24000 श्लोकस् by omitting the उपाख्यानस्-this is known as Bhārata (चतुर्विंशतिसा-हस्रीं चक्रे भारतसंहिताम् । उपाख्या-नैर् विना तावद् भारतं प्रोच्यते बुधैः) 1. 1. 61; it was further abridged into 150 श्लोकस् in the form of a table of contents of all the incidents of the sub-पर्वन्स् (this could refer to 1. 2. 71-233) (ततो ऽध्यर्धशतं भूयः संक्षेपं कृतवान् ऋषिः । अनुक्रम-णिम् अध्यायं वृत्तान्तानां सपर्वणाम् 1. 1. 62; एतद् अखिलम् आख्यातं भारतं पर्व-संग्रहात् 1. 2. 234); the list of the hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata (1. 2. 34-1. 2. 70) is included in its abridgement (समासो भारतस्यायं तत्रोक्तः पर्वसंग्रहः) 1. 2. 71; before narrating in all details, the Mahābhārata was first summarized by Vaiśampāyana for Janamejaya (कथितं वै समासेन त्वया सर्वं द्विजोत्तम । महाभारतं आख्यानम्) 1. 56. 1; this summary began with the return of the Pāṇḍavas to Hāstinapura after the death of Pāṇḍu and it ended with the death of Duryodhana and the Pāṇḍavas obtaining the kingdom 1. 55. 6-42; a sort of a sum-mary which began with Pāṇḍu's conquering many countries and then retiring to the forest and ended with the great destruction after the war leaving only ten heroes alive is made by Sūta Ugraśravas for the sages assembled in the Naimiṣa forest 1. 1. 67-158. G. Three beginnings: According to Sūta Ugraśravas there were three different views regarding the beginning of the Bhārata: (1) according to one view it began with Manu Vaivasvata (मन्वादि भारतं केचित्) 1. 1. 50 (i. e. with प्रजापतेस् तु दक्षस्य मनोर् वैवस्-वतस्य च । … अन्वये ॥ यादवानाम् इमं वंशं पौरवाणां च सर्वशः । तथैव भारतानां च (?) 1. 70. 1-2); Devabodha on 1. 1. 50 explains मनुः as आदिराजः; according to Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 1. 52, in the opinion of the easterners, मनु means मन्त्र and hence मन्वादि refers to the मङ्गल stanza नारायणं नमस्कृत्य etc. or ॐ नमो भगवते etc. found at the beginning of the epic in some manuscripts; in his own opinion, however, मनु refers to Manu Vaivasvata, the son of the heaven, cf. मनुर् मन्त्रः नारायणं नमस्कृत्येति । ॐ नमो भगवते वासुदेवायेति वा तदादि इति प्रञ्चः । दिवः पुत्रो वैवस्वतमह्य-संज्ञो मनुस् तदादीति तत्त्वम् । ); (2) according to another view the Bhārata begins with आस्तीक (आस्तीकादि तथापरे) 1. 1. 50 (i. e. with the अध्याय 1. 13 beginning of the Āstīkaparvan); (3) accor-ding to a third view it begins with उपरिचर (तथोपरिचराद् अन्ये) 1. 1. 50 (i. e. with राजोपरिचरो नाम 1. 57. 1). H. Its first teaching and subsequent narrations: (1) Teaching: Dvaipāyana (Vyāsa) first taught it to his son Śuka and then handed it over to his other deserving pupils 1. 1. 63; he taught it to Śuka together with the four श्लोकस् (18. 5. 47-50) known as the Bhārata-sāvitrī 18. 5. 51; Vyāsa taught the Mahabhā-rata to his pupils Sumantu, Jaimini, Paila, Vaiśaṃpāyana and to his son Śuka 1. 57. 74-75; Vyāsa taught it to them on the mount Meru 12. 327. 16-18; on the slope of the Himavant mountain (हिमवत्पादे) 12. 337. 9, 12, 14-15 (वेदार्थान् भारतार्थांश् च  … व्याहर्तुम् उपचक्रमे); (2) Narra-tions: (i) Nārada recited it for the gods, Asita Devala for the manes (पितृन्), and Śuka for the Gandharvas, the Yaksas and the demons 1. 1. 64; 18. 5. 42; (ii) The pupils of Vyāsa made separate public recitations of the Bhārata saṃhitā received by them from him (संहितास् तैः पृथक्त्वेन भारतस्य प्रकाशिताः) 1. 57. 75; (iii) one such reci-tation by his pupil Vaiśaṃpāyana is recorded in the epic: When Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana arrived at the snake-sacrifice of Janamejaya he was requested by the king to narrate to him the life-story of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas (1. 54. 18 ff.); भारतसावित्री: Bhāratasāvitrī f.: Name of the four stanzas (18. 5. 47-50) occurring towards the end of the Mahābhārata 18. 5. 51. The great sage Vyāsa having composed in the bygone days this Bhārata Saṃhitā, taught it to his son along with the four stanzas 18. 5. 46; contents of these stanzas (18. 5. 47-50): thousands of parents and hundreds of sons and wives with whom one lives in this world pass away and (many) others will pass away (in future) (47); only an ignorant, and not a wise person, experiences day by day thousands of occasions for delight and hundreds of occasions for fear (48); here I, (i. e. Vyāsa himself) with upraised hands, speak loudly (to people): why do you not practise धर्म since from it proceed acquisition of profit and fulfilment of desire (ऊर्ध्वबाहुर् विरौम्य् एष न च कश्चिच् छृणोति मे । धर्माद् अर्थश् च कामश् च स किमर्-थं न सेव्यते ॥ ) (49); one should not forsake धर्म for the fulfilment of desire, nor out of fear, nor greed, nor even for saving one's life; (for), धर्म is eternal, while happiness and misery are not eternal, जीव (soul) is eternal its cause (हेतु i. e. body) is not eternal (न जातु कामान् न भयान् न लोभाद् धर्मं त्यजेज् जीवि-तस्यापि हेतोः । नित्यो धर्मः सुखदुःखे त्व् अनित्ये जीवो नित्यो हेतुर् अस्य त्व् अनित्यः) (50); one who recites the Bhāratasāvitrī on waking up in the morning obtains the fruit of (reciting) the Bhārata and attains the highest ब्रह्मन् (स भारतफतं प्राप्य परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति); (according to Nīlakaṇṭha on Bom Ed. 18. 5. 60 these stanzas bring together the essence of the Bhārata and therefore deserve to be recited (तत्र पठनयोग्यं भारतसारसं-ग्रहं चतुःश्लोकीरूपम्).
भीष्मपर्वन्: Bhīṣmaparvan nt.: Name of the 6th पर्वन् in the list of the 18 major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 154, 158, 159. Described as full of varied contents (विचित्रार्थ) 1. 2. 154 and large (महा-पर्वन्) 1. 2. 158; it has 117 अध्यायस् and 5884 श्लोकस् as counted by Vyāsa (व्यासेन वेदविदुषा संख्याता भीष्म-पर्वणि) 1. 2. 159; in this पर्वन् Saṃjaya has described for Dhṛtarāṣṭra the creation of the Jambūkhaṇḍa; the terrible war lasted for ten days during which the army of Yudhiṣ-ṭhira was highly dejected; in it the highly intelligent Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa) removed the dejection arising out of confusion of Arjuna with arguments expounding salvation (कश्-मलं यत्र पार्थस्य वासुदेवो महा-मतिः । मोहजं नाशयाम् आस हेतुभिर् मोक्षदर्शनैः) 1. 2. 156 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 2. 46-47: कशमलं विषादम् । मोहजं ममतोत्थम्); in this पर्वन् Pārtha (Arjuna), placing Śikhaṇḍin in front, shot sharp arrows at Bhīṣma and felled him down from the chariot 1. 2. 155-157.
भीष्मवध: Bhīṣmavadha m.: Name of the 64th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 56, 33, 70. Referred to in the list of the contents of the Bhīṣmaparvan 1. 2. 157; also by Dhṛtarāṣṭra in his summary of the events made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 125-126; related to the अध्यायस् 6. 41-117.
भीष्मस्य: Bhīṣmasya svargārohaṇikam: Name of the 90th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃ-graha (स्वर्गारोहणिकं पर्व ततो भीष्म-स्य धीमतः) 1. 2. 65, 33, 70. Referred to in the listing of the contents of the Anuśāsanaparvan (भीष्मस्यात्रैव संप्राप्तिः स्वर्गस्य परिकीर्तिता) 1. 2. 204; related to the अध्यायस् 13. 153-154.
भीष्माभिषेचन: Bhīṣmābhiṣecana nt.: Name of the 60th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 54, 33, 70. Described as the cause of wonder (अद्भुतकारण) 1. 2. 54; related to the अध्यायस् 5. 153-156.
भूमिपर्वन्: Bhūmiparvan nt.: Name of the 62nd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 55, 33, 70. Described as attractive (मनोनुग) 6. 13. 48; in this पर्वन् the extent of the islands was described (द्वीपविस्तरकीर्तनम्) by Saṃjaya to Dhṛtarāṣṭra 1. 2. 55; related to Saṃjaya's narration in the अध्यायस् 6. 12-13; listening to the Bhūmiparvan a king becomes illustrious, achieves his objective, is honoured by the pious (श्रीमान् भवति राजन्यः सिद्धार्थः साधुसंमतः); his life, strength, energy and lustre increase (आयुर् बलं च वीर्यं च तस्य तेजश् च वर्धते) 6. 13. 48; the ancestors and grand-fathers of one who, while observing the व्रत, listens to it on the पर्वन् days are deligh-ted (प्रीयन्ते पितरस् तस्य तथैव च पितामहाः) 6. 13. 49.
भगदैव: Bhagadaiva m.: Name of the month Phalguna. Aṅgiras told Bhīṣma that one who eats only once a day in the month of Bhagadaiva (Phalguna) is loved by women and they remain under his control (भगदैवं तु यो मासम् एकभक्तेन यः क्षपेत् । स्त्रीषु वल्लभतां याति वश्याश् चास्य भवन्ति ताः) 13. 109. 21. [See Phalguna]
भगदैवत: Bhagadaivata nt.: Name of the Uttarā Phalgunī नक्षत्र; also called Bhāgya (6. 3. 14). A. Auspicious for marriage: Sage Sthūlakeśa gave Pramadvarā to Ruru fixing the marriage on the following Bhagadaivata नक्षत्र (i. e. the Uttarā Phalgunī) (विवा-हं स्थापयित्वाग्रे नक्षत्रे भगदैवते) 1. 8. 13 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 8. 16: भगदैवते पूर्वयोः फल्गुन्योर् इति लौकिकाः । फल्गुनीनक्षत्रम् अर्यमा देवता फल्गुनीनक्षत्रं भगो देवतेति श्रुतेर् उत्तराफल्गुन्योर् वा विवाहं स्था-पयित्वा निश्चित्य । ). B. Bad omen: Among the bad omens noticed by Vyāsa there was one according to which the planet Śanaiścara was afflicting the Bhāgya (i. e. the Uttarā Phalgunī) नक्षत्र (भाग्यं नक्षत्रम् आक्रम्य सूर्यपुत्रेण पीड्यते) 6. 3. 14 (Nī. who reads भगं नक्षत्रं comments on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 14: भगं नक्षत्रं पूर्वाफल्गुनी श्रुतिमते तूत्तराफल्गुनी). [See Uttarā Phalgunī]
भरणी: Bharaṇī f. (pl.): Name of a constella-tion. Religious rites: (1) दान: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that by offering sesame and cow (?तिलधेनुं प्रदाय वै) to Brāhmaṇas under Bharaṇī (भरणीषु), one obtained many cows and fame in next life 13. 63. 35 (cf., however, the note printed at the end of the अध्याय 13. 64 of the Bom. Ed.: यावता वस्त्रेण कृत्स्ना धेनुर् आच्छादिता भवति तद्वस्त्रपूरिततिलास् तिल-धेनुः); (2) श्राद्ध: Yama told Śaśa-bindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a काम्य श्राद्ध under Bharaṇī one enjoyed excellent life (आयुर् उत्तमम्) 13. 89. 14.
भाद्रपदा: Bhādrapadā f.: See Pūrvā Bhādrapadā and Uttarā Bhādrapadā.
भार्गव: Bhārgava1 m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (प्रावृषेया भार्गवाश् च) 6. 10. 49 (apparently diffe-rent from Bhārgava2).
भृग्वङ्ग: Bhṛgvaṅga(?gi)rasaka adj.: of a certain period of time. Yudhiṣṭhira asked Bhīṣma the name of the sage who first conceived of the श्राद्ध ceremony, its appropriate time and nature, in the period that was influenced by the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases (केन संकल्पितं श्राद्-धं कस्मिन् काले किमात्मकम् । भृग्व-ङ्ग(? गि)रसके काले मुनिना कतरेण वा) 13. 91. 1 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 13. 91. 1: भृग्वङ्गिरसके यदा भृगवो ऽङ्गिरसश् च वर्तन्ते नान्ये).
भद्रकर्णेश्वर: Bhadrakarṇeśvara m.: Name of a तीर्थ। By visiting it and by worshipping the god (Śiva) according to prescribed rites one does not meet with misfortune (न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्नोति) and reaches heaven 3. 82. 35.
भद्रवट: Bhadravaṭa m.: Name of a sacred place. Described as a holy place (पुण्यस्थान) and famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्) 3. 80. 69; it was sacred to Śiva 3. 80. 69; by approaching there Īśāna (Śiva) (तत्राभिगम्य चेशानम्) one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows and by the favour of Mahādeva he obtains the status of the chief of the Gaṇas (गाणपत्यम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 80. 70; when Skanda was made the chief of the army of the gods, Śiva, with Umā, proceeded to the Bhadravaṭa in a chariot to which a thousand lions were yoked (सहस्रं तस्य सिंहानां तस्मिन् युक्तं रथोत्तमे) 3. 221. 1-2.
भद्रसालवन: Bhadrasālavana nt.: Name of a forest. Situated on the eastern side of mount Meru 6. 8. 12-13; the great Kālāmra tree is in that forest 6. 8. 13.
भर्तृस्थान: Bhartṛsthāna nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as best (अनुत्तम) 3. 82. 68; 3. 83. 57; god Mahāsena (Skanda) is always present there 3. 83. 57; by bathing there in the Koṭitīrtha and by worshipping Guha (Skanda) one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows and becomes lustrous (तेजस्वी) 3. 82. 68; 3. 83. 58; one obtains perfection by just visiting it (गमनाद् एव सिध्यति) 3. 83. 58.
भारद्वाजस्य: Bhāradvājasya tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One of the तीर्थस् on the southern coast (समुद्रे तीर्थानि दक्षिणे) 1. 208. 1; 1. 209. 17; this तीर्थ, described as highly effective in causing cessation of sins (पाप-प्रशमनं महत् 1. 208. 3), was one of the five तीर्थस् which were once frequented by ascetics, but were later avoided by them due to the fear of crocodiles 1. 208. 2-4, 6; the crocodiles were in fact the Apsarases 1. 208. 14-21; Arjuna visited these तीर्थस् 1. 208. 7; he freed the तीर्थस् from the crocodiles and gave them their original form 1. 209. 19-23; all the five तीर्थस् are describ-ed as auspicious, very auspicious (पुण्यानि) 1. 209. 17, (सुपुण्यानि) 1. 208. 1; they were sanctifying for the wise (पावनानि मनीषि-णाम्) 1. 209. 11; attractive (रमणीयानि) 1. 209. 17; adorned by ascetics (शोभितानि तपस्विभिः) 1. 208. 1; all the तीर्थस्, after they would be freed from crocodiles, were to be known as Nārītīrthas (नरीतीर्थानि नाम्नेह ख्यातिं यास्यन्ति सर्वशः) 1. 209. 11. [See Nārītirthāni]
भारद्वाजी: Bhāradvājī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa (भारद्वाजीम् च निम्न-गाम्); its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 28, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
भारमर्दिनी: Bhāramardinī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 22, 13 (for other details see Bhāradvājī).
भास: Bhāsa m.: Name of a mountain. One of the twelve mountains described as kings of mountains (पर्वतराजानः) 14. 43. 4-5 (for other details see Kāṣṭhavant).
भीमरथी: Bhīmarathī f.: Name of a river. Situated in the south (दक्षिणस्याम्) 3. 86. 1; described as remover of the fear of sin (पापभयापहा), full of deer and birds (मृगद्विजसमाकीर्णा), and adorned with huts of ascetics (तापसालयभूषिता) 3. 86. 3; finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 22, 2.
भीमा: Bhīmā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 21, 13; the source of the Bhīmā is described as the best (भीमायाः स्थानम् उत्तमम्) 3. 80. 100; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā); also listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers which are declared to be mothers of the fire-hearths (i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed) 3. 212. 23 (for citation and Nī. see Kapilā); having bathed there at the source of the river (तत्र स्नात्वा तु योन्यां वै) one becomes son of a goddess with radiant gold ear-rings on his body (देव्याः पुत्रो भवेद् राजंस् तप्तकुण्डलविग्रहः) and gets the fruit of giving a hundred thousand cows 3. 80. 100-101.
भृगुतुङ्ग: Bhṛgutuṅga m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: On the Himālayan range (हिमवत्पार्श्वे) 1. 207. 1. B. Descrip-tion: Great mountain (महागिरि) 3. 88. 20; 3. 130. 16. C. Relationship with Bhṛgu: Bhṛgu, attended on by great sages, practised austerities on this mountain; the mountain then became famous as Bhṛgu's hermitage (भृगुर् यत्र तपस् तेपे … स राजन्न् आश्र-मः ख्यातो भृगुतुङ्गो महागिरिः) 3. 88. 20. D. Epic events: (1) Yudhiṣṭhira was once instructed by Rāma (Bhārgava) on this mountain (अनुशिष्टो ऽसि … भृगुतुङ्गे च रामेण) 2. 69. 12-13; (2) Arjuna, while on exile, purified himself there (कृतवाञ् शौचम् आत्मनः) 1. 207. 2 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 215. 2: भृगुतुङ्गे तुङ्गनाथ इति प्रसिद्धे); (3) Lomaśa told Yudhiṣṭhira the aggregate (of holy places 3. 129. 20-3. 130. 15) after listening to which he would soon be visiting the Bhṛgutuṅga (समाधी-नां समासस् तु पाण्डवेय श्रुतस् त्वया । तं द्रक्ष्यसि महाराज भृगुतुङ्गं महागिरिम्) 3. 130. 16 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 130. 19: समासः सङ्क्षेपः । यस्मिन् दृष्टे समाधिफलं भवतीत्य् अर्थः); later Lomaśa advised Yudhiṣṭhira to bathe quietly on this mountain together with those who lived in his house (तूष्णीम्  … सामात्यः समुपस्पृश) 3. 135. 7; (4) Departing from the Kāmyaka forest Arjuna went to the Bhṛgutuṅga and practised aus-terities; he stayed there for a night; next day, he met on his way a Brāhmaṇa who advised him to go up the mountain Himālaya to practise austerities (गिरिम् आरुह्य शैशि-रम्) 3. 163. 10, 13-14. E. Past event.: Bhṛgu practised austerities there (see section C above). F. Holiness: (1) By visit-ing the mountain one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice 3. 82. 45; (2) It is mentioned in the Tīrthavaṃśa (13. 26. 3); one who is not covetous (अलोलुपः) if he bathes in the great lake on this mountain (महाह्रद उपस्पृश्य) and fasts for three nights he is freed of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa 13. 26. 17.
भैमरथी: Bhaimarathī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 19, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
भोगवती: Bhogavatī1 f.: Name of a तीर्थ; also called Vāsukes tīrtham. Situated at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā 3. 83. 80; described as best, the तीर्थ is sacred to Vāsuki (तत्र भोग-वती नाम वासुकेस् तीर्थम् उत्तमम्) 3. 83. 81; one who bathes there gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha 3. 83. 81; one of the holy places where Ambā practised severe austeri-ties and bathed 5. 187. 26, 28; Bhogavatī, together with Prayāga and other three holy places, forms the altar of Prajāpati (प्रयागं सप्रतिष्ठानं कम्बलाश्वतरौ तथा । तीर्थं भोगवती चैव वेदी प्रोक्ता प्रजा-पतेः ॥ ) 3. 83. 72.

Bhogavatī2 f.: Name of the river Sarasvatī (?) Described as attractive (मनोरमा); Pāṇḍavas visited it and in the adjoining forest, which was the abode of ascetics, saw many perfected sages (ददर्श सिद्धर्षि-गणान् अनेकान्) 3. 25. 20 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 24. 20: भोगवतीम् सरस्वतीम् नदीम्). [See Sarasvatī]

Bhogavatī f.: Name of the city of the Nāgas. A. Location: Towards the south (दक्षिणेत्य् उच्यते ऽथ दिक् 5. 107. 1; अत्र भोगवती नाम पुरी) 5. 107. 19; below the earth, from where Śeṣa, the Nāga, holds the earth on his head (एष शेषः स्थितो नागो येनेयं धार्यते सदा … मही) 5. 101. 2. B. City of the Nāgas: It enjoyed the protection of Vāsuki (इयं भोगवती नाम पुरी वासुकिपालिता) 5. 101. 1; along with Vāsuki, it was also protected by Takṣaka and Airāvata (भोगवती नाम पुरी वासुकिपालिता । तक्षकेण च नागेन तथैवैरावतेन च ॥ ) 5. 107. 19; here the Nāgas, the sons of Surasā and Kaśyapa, lived without fear (सुरसायाः सुता नागा निवसन्ति गतव्यथाः) 5. 101. 4; (एते चान्ये च बहवः कश्यपस्यात्मजाः स्मृताः) 5. 101. 17; they were of different shapes, very large in number, strong and of fierce nature; very large in size and having large hoods, having three or more heads, even a thousand; marked with gems, स्वस्तिकस्, wheels and the shapes of कमण्डलु (मणिस्वस्तिकचक्राङ्काः कमण्डलुक-लक्षणाः) 5. 101. 5-8; some of the Nāgas living in Bhogavatī are named 5. 101. 9-16. C. Similes: (1) The city Bhoga-vatī was like the excellent city Amarā-vatī of Indra (यादृषी देवराजस्य पुरी-वर्यामरावती) 5. 101. 1; (2) (as उप-मान) (i) The excellent city of Khāṇḍava-prastha, with its white rampart, shone like Bhogavatī with its Nāgas (प्राकारेण … पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशेन हिमराशिनिभेन च । शुशुभे तत् पुरश्रेष्ठं नागैर् भोगवती यथा ॥ ) 1. 199. 30; (ii) Khāṇḍavaprastha with the five Pāṇḍavas shone like Bhoga-vatī with the Nāgas (पञ्चभिस् तैः … समन्वितम् । शुशुभे तत् पुरश्रेष्ठम् नागैर् भोगवती यथा ॥ ) 1. 199. 49 (four of the five implied Nāgas could be Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Śeṣa and Airāvata); (iii) The assembly of the kings gathered for the स्व-यंवर of Damayanti looked like Bhoga-vatī with the Nāgas (तां राजसमितिं पूर्णां नागैर् भोगवतीम् इव) 3. 54. 5.
भोगवत्: Bhogavant m.: Name of a mountain (?) Situated in the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति) 2. 26. 1; listed among the regions conquered by Bhīma (भोगवन्तं च पाण्डवः । तरसैवाजयद् भीमः) 2. 27. 11.
भोगवन्त्: Bhogavant m.: Name of a mountain (?) Situated in the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति) 2. 26. 1; listed among the regions conquered by Bhīma (भोगवन्तं च पाण्डवः । तरसैवाजयद् भीमः) 2. 27. 11.
भगस्य: Bhagasya āyatanam nt.: Nāme of a holy resort (temple ?) of Bhaga. A. Location: In a forest, not very far from the sea and the तीर्थ called Śūrpāraka (शूर्पारकं ददर्श ॥ तत्रो-दधेः कंचिद् अतीत्य देशम् … वनम् आस-साद) 3. 118. 8-9; (स तत्र … भगस्य … आयतनानि तेषां ददर्श) 3. 118. 10. 12-13. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) and very attractive (सुमनोहर) 3. 118. 13. C. Epic event: Yudhiṣṭhira visited it and many other आयतनस् in that forest; he bathed in all the तीर्थस् at the आयतनस् and observed different fasts; after giving as gifts precious gems he returned to Śūrpāraka 3. 118. 13-14.
भरतस्य: Bharatasya āśramaḥ m.: Name of the आश्रम of Bharata. On the river Kauśikī (कौशिकीं तत्र सेवेत); described as one which frees the visitor from all sins (सर्वपापप्रमोचन); by visiting it one gets the fruit of performing a Rājasūya sacrifice 3. 82. 113.
भरद्वाजाश्रम: Bharadvājāśrama m.: Name of the आश्रम of Bharadvāja. A. Description: The आश्रम had a shed for sacred fire (अग्निहोत्र 3. 137. 17; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 136. 17; अग्नि-होत्रे अग्निहोत्रशालायां; अग्न्यागार 3. 138. 7) where Bharadvāja gave offerings in fire (अग्निहोत्र) 3. 137. 17; the अग्न्या-गार was guarded by a blind शूद्र (शूद्रेणान्धेन रक्षिणा 3. 137. 18; 3. 138. 3. B. Past events: (1) When Bharadvāja, after doing the daily Vedic recitation returned to his आश्रम, the fires, as usual, did not stand up to greet him (भरद्वाजस् तु कौन्तेय कृत्वा स्वाध्या-यम् आह्निकम् … प्रविवेश स्वम् आश्रमम् ।  … पावकाः । न त्वेनम् उपतिष्ठन्ति) 3. 138. 1-2 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 137. 1: आह्निकं स्वाध्यायं प्रत्यहं कर्तव्यं ब्रह्मयज्ञम्); on enquiry, Bharadvāja was told by the blind Śūdra that as his son was trying to enter the अग्न्यागार he was stopped by him (the Śūdra) and the son was killed by a Rākṣasa 3. 137. 17-19; 3. 138. 7-8); (2) The Kāleya demons used to hide themselves in the ocean during the day; at night they used to come out and eat the sages living in holy places and आश्रमस्; once they killed twenty sages from the आश्रम of Bharadvāja who were self-contro-lled, observed celibacy, and lived on air and water (भरद्वाजाश्रमे चैव नियता ब्रह्मचारिणः । वाय्वाहाराम्बुभक्षाश् च विंशतिः संनिपातिताः) 3. 100. 1-2, 5; (3) When the Hehayas defeated king Divodāsa, he fled from his town and took shelter with Bharadvāja in his आश्रम (स त्व् आश्रमम् उपागम्य भरद्वाजस्य धीमतः । जगाम शरणं राजा) 13. 31. 23.
भरुकच्छ: Bharukaccha m.: Name of a town. Sahadeva in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1) reached it and from there he sent envoys to Paulastya Vibhīṣaṇa 2. 28. 50; the Śūdras from Bharukaccha (शूद्राः … भरुकच्छनिवासिनः) brought as tribute to Yudhiṣṭhira for his Rājasūya a hundred thousand Dāsīs, skins of Raṅku deer and horses from Gandhāra country (राङ्कवान्य् अजिनानि च । … हयान् गान्धार-देशजान्) 2. 47. 7-8.
भूतिलय: Bhūtilaya m.: Name of a village. Situated in the Bāhlīka (Āraṭṭa) country 8. 30. 40; a certain Brāhmaṇa sitting in the Sabhā of the Kauravas had said that one who bathed at Bhūtilaya could not hope to go to heaven (भूतिलये स्नात्वा कथं स्वर्गं गमिष्यति) 8. 30. 42 (accor-ding to Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 44. 41 there was a pond which was used commonly by both Caṇḍālas and Brāhmaṇas (hence it was unholy): भूतिलये हि चन्डालब्राह्मण साधारण एको जलाशयस् तत्र च स्नातः कथं स्वर्गं गच्छेन् न कथंचिद् इत्य् अर्थः); Bhūtilaya is also mentioned in an अनुवंश stanza which reports what a Piśācī told a Brāhmaṇī who, with her son(s), had come to stay on the river Raupyā; she told the Brāhmaṇī that after bathing at Bhūtilaya she could not stay near Raupyā for more than one night; and if she did stay, some calamity would over-take her at night (तद्वत् भूतिलये स्ना-त्वा सपुत्रा वस्तुम् इच्छसि ॥ एकरात्रम् उषित्वेह द्वितीयं यदि वत्स्यसि । एतद् वै ते दिवा वृत्तं रात्रौ वृत्तं अतो ऽन्यथा) 3. 129. 9-10; (according to Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 129. 9 in the opinion of the eastern critics (प्राञ्चः) Bhūlilaya was a village of the Dasyus where burnt corpses were thrown in the river (hence it was unholy), cf. भूतिलये दस्युग्रामे अग्निदग्धानां मृतानां क्षेपणं यस्यां नद्यां क्रियते तस्यां स्नातासि; according to a Dharmaśāstra stanza cited by Nī. a Brāhmaṇa who had lived in Bhūtilaya was to observe Prājāpatya vrata as an expiation: एतत्करणे प्रायश्-चित्तं धर्मशास्त्रे प्रसिद्धम् । … प्रोष्य भूलिलये विप्रः प्राजापत्यं व्रतं चरेत्; in the opinion of the critics nearer to Nī. (अर्वाञ्चः) भूलिलय meant pure ब्रह्मन् (भूतिर् ऐश्वर्यम् । तस्यापि च लयो ऽस्मिन्न् इति शुद्धं ब्रह्म) and स्नात्वा meant मलं त्यक्त्वा).
भृगोर्: Bhṛgor āśramaḥ1 m.: The आश्रम established by Bhṛgu. Past events: (1) King Yuvanāśva, who lived in forest, entered the आश्रम of Bhṛgu and drank from a jar filled with water that was sanctified with the मन्त्रस् and consecrated with austerities (संभृतो मन्त्रपूतेन वारिणा कलशो महान् 3. 126. 10; आपस् तपसा चैव संभृताः 3. 126. 18); (the waters were meant for the queen and were to cause birth of a son) 3. 126. 8, 12, 14; (2) When Bhṛgu had gone to bathe, a certain Rakṣas approached his आश्रम; entering it, he saw there Pulomā, the wife of Bhṛgu; the Rakṣas was re-ceived by Pulomā (in the आश्रम) with fruits and roots 1. 5. 13-15; the Rakṣas wanted to abduct Pulomā from the आश्रम after ascertaining from Agni that Pulomā was really the wife of Bhṛgu 1. 5. 20, 25; (3) When Vītahavya's sons were killed by Pratardana, he (Vītahavya) abandoned his city and fled to the आश्रम of Bhṛgu (प्राद्रवन् नगरं हित्वा भृगोर् आश्रमम् अप्य् उत) 13. 31. 41; Pratardana followed Vītahavya to Bhṛgu's आश्रम; he told Bhṛgu that he wanted to see his pupils living in the आश्रम; knowing this, Bhṛgu came out of the आश्रम, honoured Pratardana, and was told that there was no Kṣatriya living in the आश्रम; all the inmates of the आश्रम were twice-born; as a result, Vītahavya became a Brāhmaṇa; Pratardana was happy that he was instrumental in bringing about the change in the जाति of Vītahavya (change from क्षत्रिय to द्विज) 13. 31. 43-51. [See Cyavanasya āśramaḥ above p. 528 and Bhṛgutuṅga Vol. 1. 5, p. 400]

Bhṛgor āśramaḥ2: The आश्रम of Bhṛgu (i. e. of Bhṛguśārdūla (12. 3. 1), viz. Paraśurāma). A. Location: Near the Mahendra mountain (जगाम सहसा रामं महे-न्द्रं पर्वतं प्रति) 12. 2. 14; (महेन्द्रे पर्वतोत्तमे) 12. 2. 17; not far from the ocean (समुद्रान्ते … आश्रमान्तिके) 12. 2. 19. B. Epic event: Karṇa, who had approached Rāma for ब्रह्मास्त्र, lived in this आश्रम; once, while he was wandering on the seashore near the आश्रम he in-advertently killed the cow of a Brāhmaṇa (स कदाचित् समुद्रान्ते विचरन्न् आश्रमा-न्तिके) 12. 2. 19; Karṇa, after he received the ब्रह्मास्त्र, lived happily in the आश्रम of Bhṛgu (i. e. Rāma) (विदितास्त्रस् ततः कर्णो रममाणो ”श्रमे भृगोः) 12. 3. 3; once, while Rāma was wandering near his आश्रम with Karṇa, he slept placing his head on the lap of Karṇa (ततः कदाचित् रामस् तु चरन्न् आश्रमम् अन्तिकात् । कर्णेन सहितो … सुष्वाप … कर्णस्योत्सङ्ग आधाय शिरः) 12. 3. 4-5.
भोजकट: Bhojakaṭa nt.: Name of a city. A. Location: To the south of Hās-tinapura (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 1: (दक्षिणाभिमुखो ययौ) 2. 28. 8; (प्रायाद् विजयी दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 37; not far from Surāṣṭra country (सुराष्ट्र-विषयस्थश् च प्रेषयाम् आस रुक्मिणे) 2. 28. 40. B. Description: Excellent (उत्तम) 5. 155. 15; famous on the earth on account of its large army consisting of many elephants and horses (सैन्येन महता तेन प्रभू-तगजवाजिना । पुरं तद् भुवि विख्यातं नाम्ना भोजकटं नृप) 5. 155. 16. C. Epic event: Rukmin did not return to his former town Kuṇḍina from the place where he was defeated by Kṛṣṇa; he raised another town for himself at the place where he was defeated which came to be known as Bhojakaṭa (तत्र भोजकटं नाम चक्रे नगरम् उत्तमम्) 5. 155. 14, 15; (2) Sahadeva, while he was in Surāṣṭra, sent for Rukmin, who ruled at Bhojakaṭa; Rukmin brought jewels as tribute for the Rājasūya 2. 28. 40, 42.
भोजनगर: Bhojanagara nt.: Name of a town. Gālava, along with Mādhavī, went to Bhojanagara to see king Auśīnara (or Uśīnara 5. 116. 9, 16-17) and to get from him four hundred white horses having one black ear on one side 5. 116. 2, 5.
भद्रकार: Bhadrakāra m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned among those peoples who due to fear of Jarāsandha migrated to the west 2. 13. 24-25 (for citation see Bodha).
भरत: Bharata, Bhārata m. (pl.): General characterization of the descendants of Bharata, the son of Duḥṣanta, very often used to refer to Kauravas, or to Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas, or to Pāṇḍavas; also used as an adj. (fem. -ई) mostly to refer to the lineage or the army of the Kauravas, occa-sionally used also to refer to their narrative and town. A. Origin: The family was named Bhārata after Bharata; his descendants as well as those who preceded him (?) were known as Bhāratas; the fame of Bhāratas was due to Bharata (भरताद् भाराती कीर्तिर् येनेदं भारतं कुलम् । अपरे ये च पूर्वे च भारता इति विश्रुताः) 1. 69. 49; 1. 89. 16; 13. 75. 26; (1. 1. 44). B. Line-age (वंश or कुल), its importance: Since the lineage was established by Bharatas it was known as Bhārata (येनेदं (i. e. भरतेन) भारतं कुलम्) 1. 69. 49; भारतं वंशम् 1, 99. 47; Arjuna born in the lineage of Bharata (जातस्य भारते वंशे) 2. 16. 1; Duryodhana born in the lineage of Bharata (जातो ऽसि भारते वंशे) 5. 7. 27; (भार-तं कुलं) 1. 69. 49; 1. 92. 12; it was respected by all kings (भारते वंशे सर्वपार्थिवपूजिते) 5. 7. 27. C. The narrative of Bhāratas, its importance: Vaiśaṃpāyana having received it from his teacher Vyāsa was eager to narrate the narrative of Bhāratas to Janamejaya, who was a worthy person to listen to it (श्रोतुं पात्रं च राजंस् त्वं प्राप्येमां भार-तीं कथाम् । गुरोर् वक्तुं परिस्पन्दो मुदा प्रोत्साहतीव माम् ॥ ) 1. 55. 3; it was told in the सर्पसत्र of king Jana-mejaya (कथेयम् … भारतानाम्) 1. 2. 74; one who listened to the narration of the birth of Bhāratas has no fear from diseases, least of all of the next world; it was holy, brought wealth, fame, long life and heaven; it is also large and leads to bliss (भारतानां महज् जन्म शृण्वताम्  … । नास्ति व्याधिभयं तेषां परलोक-भयं कुतः ॥ धन्यं यशस्यम् आयु-ष्यं स्वर्ग्यं पुण्यं तथैवच) 1. 56. 24-25; (वंशं … । तथैव भारतानां च पुण्यं स्वस्त्ययनं महत् । धन्यं यशस्यम् आयुष्यं कीर्तयिष्यामि ते ऽन-घ ॥ ) 1. 70. 2; Mahābhārata so called because it describes the life of the Bhāratas; that is the etymology of the word (भारता-नां महज् जन्म महाभारतम् उच्यते । निरुक्तम् अस्य यो वेद) 1. 56. 31. D. Description of Bhāratas: Magnanimous (महात्मन्) 1. 2. 74; 7. 61. 34; famous (भारता इति विश्रुताः) 1. 69. 49; (प्र-ख्यात) 1. 92. 12; (भरतवंशस्य विप्रतस्थे महद् यशः) 1. 89. 16; best men (उत्तमपुरुष) 2. 64. 8. E. Epic events: (1) Bhīṣma after defeating the kings who came for the स्वयंवर of the Kāśi princesses left for Bhāratas (i. e. to the place where Bhāratas lived) (प्रायाद् भारतो भारतान् प्रति) 1. 96. 24; (2) Satyavatī asked Ambikā to bear a son (from Vyāsa) and rescue the Bhārata dynasty 1. 99. 47-48; (3) Satyavatī asked Bhīṣma to get consecrated as a king and rule the Bhāratas 1. 97. 11; (4) Satyavatī told Ambikā that due to the wrong policy of her son, Bhāratas and their relatives would perish 1. 119. 9 (that is what she had heard from Vyāsa 1. 119. 5); (5) Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas born in the lineage of Bharata (भरतस्यान्वये जाता॥) 1. 122. 15; (6) Bhīṣma told Duryodhana that if Pāṇḍa-vas did not get a share in the kingdom, neither could he nor any other Bhārata have one (कुत एव तवापीदं भारतस्य च कस्यचित्) 1. 195. 6; (7) When Kṛṣṇa arrived, the town of Bharatas (i. e. Indra-prastha भारतं पुरम्) was delighted 2. 30. 15; (8) When Draupadī was dragged to the Sabhā, she felt that the law of Bhāratas had perished (नष्टः खलु भारतानाम् धर्मस् … ) 2. 60. 33; (9) Vidura felt that the end of Bharatas had arrived when Draupadī was brought to their Sabhā (एतदन्ताः स्थ भरता … ) 2. 72. 27; (10) When Bhīma vowed to break the thigh of Duryodhana Vidura felt that the unlawful course, ordained before by the fate, was proving true for the Bharatas (Kauravas) (दैवेरितो नूनम् अयं पुरस्तात् परो ऽनयो भरतेषूदपादि) 2. 63. 16; (11) Arjuna reminded Bhīma, that the Bhāratas, since they were best men, did not answer back the harsh words, spoken or unspoken, by low men (न चैवोक्ता न चानुक्ता हीनतः परुषा गिरः । भारताः प्रतिजल्पन्ति सदा तूत्तम-पूरुषाः) 2. 64. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 72. 8: प्रतिजल्पन्ति प्रत्युत्तरयन्ति); (12) The bad omens which occurred when Pāṇḍavas started for वनवास predicted extinction of Bhāratas (भारतानाम् अभा-वाय) 2. 71. 28; (13) When Duryodhana and others sought refuge with Droṇa, he addressed them as well as the rest of the Bhāratas present in the Sabhā 2. 71. 33; (14) Yudhiṣṭhira took leave of Bharatas like Bhīṣma, Bāhlīka Somadatta, and others (which included all those who sided with Kauravas) to go to वनवास (आमन्त्र-यामि भरतांस् तथा वृद्धं पितामहम्) 2. 69. 1; (15) Dhṛtarāṣṭra remembered that all Bhārata women, together with Gāndhārī, had cried fiercely when Draupadī was taken to Sabhā (प्राक्रोशन् भैरवं तत्र) 2. 72. 19; (16) If Duryodhana did not give Pāṇḍavas their share, that would bring calamity to Bharatas (भरतानाम् अभूतये) 3. 30. 48; भार्ग: Bhārga m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (पुण्ड्रा भार्गाः किराताश् च) 6. 10. 49.
भृगु: Bhṛgu m. (pl.), Bhārgava2 (adj.): Descendants of the sage Bhṛgu; often men-tioned along with Aṅgirases. A. Importance: Aṅgiras, Kaśyapa, Vasiṣṭha and Bhṛgu were recognized as the four original गोत्रस् (originators of the lineage) (मूलगोत्राणि चत्वारि) 12. 285. 17; the excellent lineage of Bhṛgus honoured by gods including Indra, Agni and the Maruts (देवैः … । पूजितः प्रवरो वंशो भृगूणाम्) 1. 5. 5; Bhṛgus reckoned among the world's foremost Brāhmaṇas (सर्वस्य जगतः श्रेष्ठा ब्राह्मणाः) 3. 27. 8. B. Description: Learned in the Vedas (वेद-विदां … भृगूणाम्) 1. 169. 11; enjoying precedence over others (अग्रभुज्) 1. 169. 12; meditative (भावितात्मन्) 1. 170. 15; 13. 56. 14; Bhṛgus were known to get very angry (भृगवो ह्य् अतिरोषणाः) 14. 96. 7; while fighting, they used black deerskins as their banners (कृष्णाजिनध्वजाः) 13. 34. 17. C. History of Bhṛgus: The detailed lineage of Bhṛgu described by Sūta to Śaunaka in the Paulomaparvan (cf. 1. 2. 34) since Śaunaka desired to hear it (1. 5. 3) (पौलोमे भृगुवंशस्य विस्तारः परिकीर्तितः) 1. 2. 72 (i. e. अध्यायस् 1. 5-12); 1. 5. 6; 1. 53. 27-28; D. Epic events; (1) Sages of different families among whom are mentioned Bhṛgus, Aṅgirases and others, protected by Yudhiṣṭhira, observed व्रतस् (धृतव्रताः) and followed their धर्म in the Dvaitavana (चरन्ति धर्मं … ) 3. 27. 7-8; (2) Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases are mentioned among the ascetics (तापसान्) who were honoured by Yudhiṣṭhira on the Mahendra mountain 3. 115. 2; (3) Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases mentioned among those sages who appeared on the battle-field to blame Droṇa since he fought against धर्म; they told him it was time for him to abandon life (अधर्मतः कृतं युद्धं समयो निधनस्य ते) 7. 164. 88-89. E. Past events: (1) Bhṛgus acted as priests in the sacrifices of Kṛtavīrya (also cf. 13. 56. 2); he gave them corn and wealth at the end of Soma sacrifices (धान्येन च धनेन च); after the death of Kṛtavīrya, his kinsmen, when in need of money, asked eminent Bhṛgus to give it since they knew Bhṛgus had wealth; some Bhṛgus, afraid of Kṣatriyas, parted with their wealth, but others hid it underground; when one of the kings was digging the ground he, by chance, found wealth in the house of a Bhṛgu; the assembled Kṣatriyas, due to anger, disregarded the supplications of the Bhṛgus and killed them all with sharp arrows; they killed even children, yet unborn (आ गर्भाद् अनुकृन्तन्तश् … ) (also cf. 13. 56. 3); when Bhṛgus were thus being extirpated their wives took shelter in mountain Himavant; one of them held her embryo in her thigh for the conti-nuation of the line of her husband (तासाम् अन्यतमा गर्भं भयाद् दाधार तैज-सम् । ऊरुणैकेन वामोरूर् भर्तुर् कुल-विवृद्धये ॥ ); when the embryo came out breaking the thigh he deprived the Kṣatrī-yas of their eyesight; the Kṣatriyas begged pardon of the Bhṛgu wife 1. 169. 11-22; the Bhṛgupatnī told the Kṣatriyas that she had not deprived them of their eyesight; that was done by the angry Bhārgava (Aurva); since the Kṣatriyas started killing even the unborn Bhṛgus she had held her embryo in the thigh for a hundred years; in order to do a favour to the Bhṛgu line-age, the entire Veda along with the six Vedāṅgas entered her child even when he was unborn; the child angered by the death of his ancestors (Bhṛgus) at the hands of Kṣatriyas had deprived them of their eyesight and wished to kill them 1. 170. 1-5; Aurva told the Kṣatriyas born in the lineage of Kṛtavīrya that while he was in the thigh of his mother he had heard the cry of his mothers (आरावं मातृवर्गस्य भृगूणां) due to the killings of Kṣatriya; he was angered because the wretched Kṣatriyas killed Bhṛgus not sparing even those unborn; when nobody offered shelter to the wives of Bhṛgus due to fear, one of them had concealed him in her thigh (1. 171. 5, 6, 8); Aurva practised severe penance to take revenge of the Bhṛgus who were killed by destroying the worlds; he thought he would delight the dead Bhṛgus (इच्छन्न् अपचितिं कर्तुं भृगूणां भृगुसत्तमः 1. 170. 11; Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 1. 179. 10: आत्मनो मनः सर्वेषां अपचितिं कर्तुं प्रवणं उन्मुखं इच्छन् स्व-मनोपचितिं कर्तुं योजयतीत्य् अर्थः); the dead Bhṛgus then descended from the world of Fathers (पितृलोकाद् उपागम्य) and asked him to control his anger; they assured him that the Bhṛgus disregarded their getting killed by Kṣatriyas not because of their weakness; they preferred getting killed by Kṣatriyas because they themselves were tired of their long life (आयुषा हि प्रकृष्टेन यदा नः खेद आविशत् । तदा-स्माभिर् वधस् तात क्षत्रियैर् ईप्सितः स्वयम् ॥ ); some one hid wealth in the house of a Bhṛgu in order to anger Kṣatri-yas; Bhṛgus desired heaven, and had no longing for wealth, however, death was powerless to overtake Bhṛgus and suicide would deprive them from getting good worlds; hence they found some other way out (to get killed by Kṣatriyas); what Aurva had wanted to achieve by the exercise of his penance was not approved by Bhṛgus; so they asked him to desist from doing the sinful act of destroying the worlds 1. 170. 11-21; (2) Cyavana told Kuśika the above account and added that due to the energy of Bhṛgus (भृगू-णाम् एव तेजसा) in his dynasty his grand-son would be an ascetic Brāhmaṇa (विप्र for विप्रः ?) having the lustre of fire; he also told him that a matrimonial alliance would be established between him (Kuśi-ka's line) and the Bhṛgus (भविता त्वं च संबन्धी भृगूणां भावितात्मनाम्) 13. 56. 1-14); (भृगूणां कुशिकानां च प्रति संबन्धकारणम्) 13. 56. 19; (3) Rāma Jāmadagnya filled at Samantapañ-caka five ponds with blood of Kṣatriyas where he offered libations to his fore-fathers (i. e. Bhṛgus) (त्रिःसप्तकृत्वः पृथिवीं कृत्वा निःक्षत्रियां प्रभुः । समन्तपञ्चके पञ्च चकार रुधिरह्र-दान् ॥ स तेषु तर्पयाम् आस पितॄन् भृगु-कुलोद्वहः) 3. 117. 9-10; (4) Vāyu told Arjuna (Kārtavīrya) that he would face in future a great danger from the Bhṛgus (भृगुभ्यस् ते भयं घोरं … ) 13. 142. 23; (5) As an instance of the super-iority of Brahmanical lustre and strength over that of the Kṣatriyas was cited the past event of Bhṛgus defeating Tālajaṅghas (भृगवो ऽजयंस् तालजङ्घान्) 13. 34. 16; (6) Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases mentioned among those who attended the anointment of Skanda as the leader of the army of the gods 9. 44. 8; (7) At the Raudra मुहूर्त Indra saw in the east Agni entering the sun with offerings which were offered by Aṅgirases and Bhṛgus 3. 213. 29. भोज: Bhoja m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people; they form a tribe of the Yādavas, but once mentioned separately from Yādavas (2. 55. 6); often mentioned along with Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, and sometimes also with Kukuras; styled as Mahābhoja (1. 213. 34). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (चेदिवत्साः करूषाश् च भोजाः … ) 6. 10. 30. B. Origin and history: (1) Bhojas originate from Druhyu (one of the sons of Yayāti) (द्रुह्योर् अपि सुता भोजा) 1. 80. 26; according to a curse pronounced on Druhyu by Yayāti, he (Druhyu) and his progeny were to be designated भोज but not ‘king’ (अराजा भोजशब्दं त्वं तत्रा-वाप्स्यसि सान्वयः) 1. 79. 19; (2) Bhojas, who have their origin in Yayāti, extended far and wide to the four corners; all kings respected their glory (तेषां तथैव तां लक्ष्मीं सर्वक्षत्रम् उपासते); in that line Caturyu Jarāsaṃdha was the hundred and first king (चतुर्युस् त्व् अपरो राजा यस्मिन्न् एकशतो ऽभवत् । स … जरासन्धः) 2. 13. 6-8; the elderly kings of Bhojas, harassed by Kaṃsa, came to an under-standing with Yādavas, since they wanted to save their kinsmen (भोजराजन्य वृद्धैस् तु … ज्ञातित्राणम् अभीप्सद्भिर् अस्मत्संभावना कृता) 2. 13. 31-32; (3) Bhojas said to have originated from Akrūra and Bhoja (i. e. Āhuka ? cf. 12. 82. 10) (अक्रूरभोजप्रभवाः सर्वे ह्य् एते तद-न्वयाः) 12. 82. 14. C. Description: Proud (मानिन्) 8. 51. 16; of great vigour (परमौजस्) 4. 67. 24; magnanimous (महात्मन्), proud like a lion (सिंह-दर्प), brave (शूर), of great strength (महाबल), whose arms resembled iron-bars and could bear attacks with maces and iron-bars (गदापरिघशक्तीनां सहाः परिघबाहवः), having strong arms (बाहुशालिन्) 16. 9. 9-11; cruel, rough in battles (क्रूर, संग्रामकर्कश) 8. 15. 10; great chariot-fighters (महारथ) 6. 20. 14; 16. 2. 1; 18. 4. 14; their army difficult to pass through (भोजानीकं च दुस्तरं) 7. 69. 1; 7. 76. 13; 7. 96. 8; devoted to Kṛṣṇa (भोजाः … त्वय्य् आसक्ता … ) 12. 82. 29; D. Epic events: (1) Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, curious to see Arjuna, gathered together when he visited Dvārakā; they all welcomed him and when Arjuna bowed down to those who deserved that honour, they greeted him; their youngsters honoured him; Arjuna embraced those who were of his age 1. 210. 17-20; Bhojas and others once held a festival on the Raivataka mountain 1. 211. 2; (after the abduction of Subhadrā) they were agitated when they heard the sound of the war-drum; they left eating and drinking and gathered in the Sudharmā hall (सभापालो भेरीं सांनाहिकीं ततः । समाजघ्ने … क्षुब्धास् तेनाथ शब्देन भोज° … । अन्नपानम् अपास्याथ समापेतुः सभां ततः) 1. 212. 11-12 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 220. 11: सांनाहिकीं संनद्धाः सर्वे भवतेति सूचयन्तीम्); Bhojas and others followed Balarāma when he decided to fight with Arjuna (तं … अन्वपद्यन्त ते सर्वे) 1. 212. 32 (Nī. on 1. 220. 32: अन्वपद्यन्त अनुमोदितवन्तः); Bhojas and others went to Khāṇḍavaprastha to give nuptial gifts after the marriage of Subhadrā; Kṛṣṇa along with Mahābhojas and others entered the city Khāṇḍava-prastha (केशवः । वृष्ण्यन्धकमहा-भोजैः संवृतः) 1. 213. 29, 34; (2) When Bhoja Kṣatriyas (भोजराजन्यान्) had gone for sport to the Raivataka mountain, Śiśupāla attacked them, slew (some of) them and took them captive to his city 2. 42. 8; (3) Bhojas, Andhakas and Yādavas parted company with Kaṃsa and lived happily for a hundred years when Kṛṣṇa killed him (अन्धका यादवा भोजाः समेताः कंसम् अत्यजन् ॥ … हते तस्मिन्  … सर्वे मोदमानाः शतं समाः) 2. 55. 6-7; (4) When Bhojas and others heard of Pāṇḍavas' exile, they came to the Dvaita-vana to meet and console them 3. 13. 1; (5) Sātyaki suggested to Balarāma to wage war with Kauravas so that the army consisting of the principal warriors (योधमुख्याः) of Bhojas and others might kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and attain wide fame (लोके यशः स्फीतम् उपाकरोतु) 3. 120. 19;
